conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, this is Officer Davis from the Collections Department. How can I assist you today?
Uh, yes. I got a message about some kind of IRS refund for veterans? I just wanted to check if this is real.

Yes, Mr. Thomas, you are eligible for a federal tax refund as part of the Veterans Relief Stimulus. Our records show you are owed $3,700, but there's a verification step required by the IRS before funds are released.
Okay... What sort of verification do you need? I've had scams try to target my pension before.

I understand your concern. This is a mandatory IRS identity and clearance process. Before we can issue your refund, you must pay a one-time processing fee of $299. It's government protocol to prevent fraud.
I don't know... I thought refunds just get sent to my bank automatically.

Normally, yes, but due to recent increases in tax fraud, the IRS now requires this clearance payment for all veteran refunds over $2,000. If you do not complete this today, your refund will be permanently forfeited and you may be flagged for review.
Flagged for review? Does that mean an audit or something?
It could result in an audit of your previous tax returns or even a hold on your social security benefits. I strongly advise you to act quickly.
Alright. How do I pay this fee? I don't want any trouble.

For your safety, the IRS only accepts secure clearance payments for this program through Apple or Target gift cards. You'll need to purchase $299 in gift cards and read the codes to me for processing.
Gift cards? That sounds odd for the IRS.

These are IRS-approved prepaid instruments used for immediate clearance. If you hesitate, your refund will be denied and you may face penalties. I'm not authorized to hold your file for more than 30 minutes.
I guess I can go to the store, but I don't drive anymore. Can my daughter help me get them?
No, you must not involve any third parties for security reasons. Take your ID and pension card to your nearest Target or CVS. Call me immediately once you have the gift cards.
Alright, I can arrange for a taxi. Do I need to get three $100 cards, or one $299 card?
Three $100 cards is acceptable. Make sure they are Apple or Target cards, and do not let the cashier know what they're for. This is a confidential IRS process.
Okay, I'll try to get them. Do you need any information from me first?
Yes. For security, verify your full name, date of birth, and the last four digits of your Social Security Number.
It's James Thomas, born July 17, 1952. Last four of my SSN are 4456.
Thank you, Mr. Thomas. Write down this reference number: IRX-8842. You'll need it when you report back with the codes.
Alright, I've written it down. I'm heading out now.
Do not disconnect this call until you have purchased the gift cards. If you hang up or delay, your file will be flagged and your entire pension may be frozen.
I understand. I'll keep the call on speaker as I go.
Good. Once you have the cards, scratch off the silver strip and read me the numbers. You must complete this within 30 minutes, or the IRS will suspend your refund and notify law enforcement.
I'm at the store now. Getting the cards.
Excellent. Once you have them, stay on the line and tell me the codes immediately. Do not share this information with anyone else.
Okay, I have the cards. Ready to give you the numbers.
Read each code slowly and clearly so I can verify your payment and release your IRS refund. Go ahead with the first code.
